themes_detail.label: Underground Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints spiked 567% THIS WEEK (5 complaints vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), coinciding with repeated city budget requests for sanitary sewer development—signaling a potential widespread subsurface failure affecting streets and private property.
evidence: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 average (z-score: 5.13, 567% increase)
Lot Condition complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 average (z-score: 4.41, 700% increase)—suggests broader ground instability
Community board repeatedly requests DEP capital project for 'street segments currently lacking sanitary sewers'—indicating known infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Investigate which specific streets or blocks are experiencing the spike; obtain city maintenance records to determine if there's deferred work
Interview residents about property damage (collapsed driveways, burst pipes); connect to CB budget requests to show this is a documented, unfunded problem

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Sanitation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped 300% THIS PAST WEEK (6 complaints vs. 1.5 weekly average), while unsanitary animal conditions on private property surged 264% LAST WEEK (5 complaints vs. 1.4 average)—suggesting possible disease vector or environmental breakdown in waste management.
evidence: Dead Animal complaints: 6 LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.18, 300% increase)
Unsanitary Animal Private Property complaints: 5 LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.26, 264% increase)
Overall Unsanitary Condition complaints rank #8 in 90-day volume (375 total), suggesting chronic sanitation challenges
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH and Parks Dept for reports of disease outbreaks or pest infestations; determine if a specific neighborhood block is the cluster
Interview residents near spike locations about health concerns; check if rodent baiting or cleanup services have been delayed or withdrawn

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street signs spiked 281% three weeks ago (10 complaints vs. 2.6 weekly average) and street condition complaints remain among the top 5 complaint types (954 total over 90 days), signaling accelerating public realm neglect and potential safety hazards.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling complaints: 10 three weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.24, 281% increase)
Street Condition complaints: 954 total over 90 days, ranking #5 complaint type district-wide
420 DOB building permits filed (231 alterations), suggesting ongoing construction activity that may be exacerbating street damage
reporting_angles: Audit DOE and FDOT data on street maintenance schedules; determine if repair work is deferred or understaffed
Document dangling signs, potholes, and cracked sidewalks with photos; identify patterns by council district or neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Public Safety & Policing Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints surged 273% TWO WEEKS AGO (7 complaints vs. 1.9 weekly average), and Emergency Response Team complaints jumped 380% (3 complaints vs. 0.6 average), with panhandling complaints up 400% (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 average)—indicating potential public safety or street disorder escalation.
evidence: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints: 7 two weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.34, 273% increase)
Emergency Response Team complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 3.41, 380% increase)
Panhandling complaints: 5 two weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.58, 400% increase)
reporting_angles: Request NYPD complaint data and incident reports for the specific week; interview precinct leadership about whether staffing or policy changed
Speak with residents, business owners, and advocates about the nature of complaints; determine if spike reflects actual behavior change or increased reporting

themes_detail.label: Heat & Hot Water Emergency (Seasonal)
themes_detail.summary: Heat/Hot Water complaints dominate the district with 1,338 complaints over 90 days, ranking #1 by far—a persistent seasonal crisis in a district with aging infrastructure and significant development activity (420 DOB permits), raising questions about landlord compliance and building code enforcement.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water complaints: 1,338 total over 90 days—by far the #1 complaint type in CD 414
420 active DOB permits (231 alterations) suggest ongoing building work that may disrupt heating systems
Recurring CB budget request for 'Other expense budget request for DEP' indicates heating infrastructure is a known, unfunded problem
reporting_angles: Request HPD violation and compliance data; determine which buildings or landlords have chronic heat violations and what enforcement action has been taken
Profile a family without heat during winter; connect to broader narrative about aging housing stock and landlord neglect in Far Rockaway
